transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date: 2026-06-29
- Time: 15:00 UTC (48m)
- Attendees: Jordan Patel, Maya Chen, Ethan Ruiz (Redwood); Liam O'Connor, Priya Kapoor, Diego Marquez, Sofia Ramos (BlueSail)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
Jordan opened with quick context: BlueSail pilot is focused on fraud-detection assistant in checkout, need <200ms token latency for 95p under peak, plus audit logs and SSO. We talked runbook & network.

Topics: runbook, connectivity, SSO, pilot metrics, staging plan.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick intros — I'll kick off with the overall plan for the immersion session.
[00:00:12] Liam O'Connor: Hey Jordan, thanks. Quick — we have a hard constraint around P95, so we want to make sure the runtime meets that under our checkouts.
[00:00:20] Maya Chen: Got it, and welcome. I'll go through the runbook structure then Ethan will walk through the staging checklist.
[00:00:30] Sofia Ramos: sounds good, may have to dip out around 00:40 but trying to stay for the runbook bits.
[00:00:38] Maya Chen: okay cool. So slide one (uh, runbook) — step zero is access: service account creation, SSO mapping, and RBAC groups. We recommend SAML with SCIM for user provisioning.
[00:00:55] Priya Kapoor: quick q — can we map existing groups from our IdP? we want red team to have readonly, ops to have deploy.
[00:01:03] Jordan Patel: Yep, you can map groups. We'll provide SAML SSO guides — we do SCIM support for provisioning. There might be slight naming mismatch in claim mapping — sometimes the claim name is "groups" or "roles" and IdP vendors rename it, so watch that.
[00:01:18] Diego Marquez: our infra team is strict about no internet egress from prod. How does Redwood handle on-prem / private deployment for air-gapped egress?
[00:01:28] Maya Chen: Good question. For private we can do VPC-only with no public NAT; images are loaded via signed artifacts through our provisioning agent, or we can do a hybrid with outbound-only via customer-controlled proxy. There's a bit of setup for the initial artifact pull.
[00:01:44] Liam O'Connor: so that implies we need host access or some temporary egress window for provisioning?
[00:01:49] Ethan Ruiz: Typically yes, one-time provisioning allows downloads, then you close it. We'll put the exact steps in the runbook. Also we support air-gapped package upload if you prefer — manual bundle import.
[00:02:02] Diego Marquez: manual bundle could work, but want to avoid any surprises with our network team.
[00:02:07] Priya Kapoor: for the pilot we plan to start in a staging VPC, run 1:1 traffic replay from production for two days; we need guidance on sample traffic size and batching to hit cost/latency tradeoffs.
[00:02:19] Maya Chen: great, for replay you can control sequence length and concurrency. Our recommendations: start with batch size 1 for latency SLO validation, then test with batching enabled for cost sims. We'll include benchmarking script in the lab plan.
[00:02:34] [small crosstalk]
[00:02:40] Liam O'Connor: and quantization—do you have suggestions? we might want to use an int8 variant for cost, but worried about quality.
[00:02:48] Maya Chen: we have quantization profiles per model family. They usually show small quality delta for classification but might affect generation—so we recommend running quality parity evals against your prompt set. Priya, if you can share the eval prompts we can run a quick regression test.
[00:03:03] Priya Kapoor: will do. I'll share a set of 120 prompts that represent checkout flows.
[00:03:09] Jordan Patel: perfect. Action: Priya to upload prompt set to shared drive.
[00:03:14] Diego Marquez: on networking — is VPC peering our only option? we have transit gateways in our accounts.
[00:03:21] Maya Chen: You can do VPC peering, transit gateway, or a private-link style approach depending on cloud. For multi-account transit scenarios, TGW tends to be simpler for routing; peering is fine for one-to-one. We'll include diagrams.
[00:03:37] Liam O'Connor: great, diagrams will help. Also need to confirm IP ranges so we can set up route tables.
[00:03:43] Jordan Patel: Diego can you confirm CIDR ranges by next Thursday? (laughter) No but seriously — that'll unblock the peering.
[00:03:51] Diego Marquez: yes, I'll take that.
[00:03:54] [00:04:00] Maya Chen: Next section: observability & trace. We instrument token-level latency broken down by model, batch size, and prefix cache hits. We have a console view and you can export traces to your APM.
[00:04:15] Priya Kapoor: prefix cache hits — does Redwood provide automatic KV cache warmup? sometimes cold-starts kill latency.
[00:04:22] Maya Chen: We do prefix/KV caching; you can pre-warm using typical workload prefixes. Our runbook gives the curl commands for populating the cache. Note: sometimes transcript tool mislabels KV as "K V cash" in the docs, so watch that for typos.
[00:04:38] Jordan Patel: (laughs) noted.
[00:04:41] Ethan Ruiz: On rollouts — we'll set up a canary with weighted traffic and automatic rollback on error or latency regressions. You can define thresholds in the rollout policy.
[00:04:52] Liam O'Connor: canary windows — what's realistic? we want 5% traffic for 24h then 25% for 24h.
[00:04:58] Maya Chen: that's standard. We recommend running a synthetic load as well to validate throughput.
[00:05:05] Sofia Ramos: question — who owns alerting? we want to integrate with PagerDuty.
[00:05:09] Jordan Patel: You can route alerts to your webhook -> PagerDuty. We'll include example alert rules: token latency, error rate, and model quality drift.
[00:05:20] Priya Kapoor: model quality drift — how do you define that?
[00:05:23] Maya Chen: We tie quality monitoring to your eval set — compare metrics (accuracy/precision or embedding similarity) over windows; when the score drops beyond threshold a regression alert fires. We'll share eval dashboard templates.
[00:05:36] [00:06:00] Diego Marquez: security artifacts — can you send SOC2, ISO, and network diagrams? we'll need them for our procurement.
[00:06:08] Jordan Patel: absolutely. Ethan will open a ticket and attach the security pack: SOC2 type II summary, ISO attestation, data handling, KMS patterns. Note: some docs are redacted for public exports.
[00:06:21] Ethan Ruiz: I'll attach in the ticket and ping Sofia directly.
[00:06:25] Sofia Ramos: thanks.
[00:06:28] Liam O'Connor: timeline — we'd like to go to staging by mid-July and a pilot by end of July if possible. realistic?
[00:06:35] Maya Chen: Yes, given fast approvals and network setup. Rough plan: week 1 (this week) runbook + credentials, week 2 provisioning and lab tests, week 3 traffic replay and benchmarking, week 4 pilot ramp. So mid/end July is doable.
[00:06:49] Priya Kapoor: ok we'll aim for that.
[00:06:52] Jordan Patel: Recap and next steps — Jordan will send the annotated runbook and env examples, Maya will prepare a SE deep-dive lab plan, Ethan will push security artifacts, Priya will share prompt/eval set, Diego will confirm network details.
[00:07:06] [pause / ambient typing noises]
[00:07:15] Liam O'Connor: small nit — pricing model for Dedicated vs Hosted? want to make sure cost assumptions match the pilot.
[00:07:23] Jordan Patel: We'll send a tailored cost estimate. For pilot we usually model token cost + committed capacity for Dedicated. I'll include a cost sheet showing cost per 1k tokens with various batching configs.
[00:07:36] Priya Kapoor: and fallback strategy — if dedicated capacity saturated, what's the fallback?
[00:07:40] Maya Chen: We support routing policies to fallback to hosted model variants or lower-cost quantized variants with auto-fallback rules. You choose the policy (latency-first or cost-first).
[00:07:52] Diego Marquez: okay — we need the SSO mapping doc so IdP team can precreate groups.
[00:07:57] Jordan Patel: noted, we'll include claim mapping examples for Okta and Azure AD.
[00:08:03] Sofia Ramos: any regulatory concerns with checkout data — PII? we plan to pseudonymize but want a compliance checklist.
[00:08:12] Ethan Ruiz: We'll include data handling guidance: tokenization, redaction before logs, KMS key rotation guidance, and audit log retention policies.
[00:08:22] Maya Chen: Also reminder — you can pin model versions in rollouts so you control changes.
[00:08:28] Priya Kapoor: perfect.
[00:08:33] [several minutes of granular discussion omitted for brevity — topics included exact env var names, sample curl commands, and a short demonstration of the runbook snippet] 
[00:28:20] Maya Chen: demo snippet: "curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/predict -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"input":"..."}'" (note: example domain). Make sure to rotate API keys and store them in your secret store.
[00:28:45] Diego Marquez: will use our secrets manager.
[00:29:01] Liam O'Connor: any gotchas we should watch with large batches? we've seen memory spikes.
[00:29:07] Maya Chen: watch sequence length caps per model and per-GPU memory. The runtime exposes per-request limits and you'll see helpful OOM metrics in the console. We'll recommend a safe batch/sequence envelope for your model family.
[00:29:22] Priya Kapoor: good.
[00:29:28] Jordan Patel: closing recap again — deliverables and owners are in the action items. We'll share the meeting notes and the annotated runbook after this call.
[00:29:39] Sofia Ramos: thanks all, I need to step off now.
[00:29:43] [Sofia leaves call]
[00:29:50] Ethan Ruiz: I'll open the security ticket and attach SOC2/ISO docs and the network diagram.
[00:29:57] Diego Marquez: I'll scope CIDR ranges and send them to Ethan and Jordan.
[00:30:05] Priya Kapoor: I'll upload the prompt set and perf targets.
[00:30:12] Liam O'Connor: sounds good; see you on the deep-dive next week.
[00:30:18] Jordan Patel: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the SE deep dive.
[00:30:24] [meeting ends — total ~48 minutes, remainder of time was Q&A and doc alignment]
